claim_scope_statement: Bounded schedule exploration under the bounds below is systematic concurrency testing, never proof (assurance/concurrency/plan.json claim ceiling). Native-thread stress samples schedules without coverage accounting and cannot stand in for the systematic result, nor the systematic result for native-thread evidence.
recorded_at_provenance: captured from `date -u` immediately before this revision was written; the counters below are transcribed verbatim from the US017_EXPLORATION line printed by `cargo test -p ws-driver --release --test schedule_exploration bounded_exploration -- --nocapture`, and the retention entries from the US017_RETENTION lines of the retention test, both on the tree being committed
revision_note: supersedes the dabb5d6 revision after owner decision us017-repeated-eof-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha f6270948), which AMENDS the bd7849c3 decision's retention of the eof_applied latch. FOURTH defect of one shape closed: a REPEATED DriverInput::TransportEof (or a Shutdown after an applied EOF) was skipped by `&& !self.eof_applied`, so the core never saw it. DriverInput::TransportEof is a SCORED EVENT, not an idempotent transport fact the adapter may absorb; at-most-once APPLICATION was the wrong invariant at the driver layer. The eof/shutdown flags are now PER-NOTIFICATION: cleared when the core consumes the EOF, re-armed by any later notification, and deliberately RETAINED on a non-fatal refusal, which is what preserves the eof-backpressure-livelock fix. COUNTERS RE-MEASURED, NOT CARRIED OVER: far more schedules now surface a typed failure, because a repeat EOF/shutdown that used to be swallowed is answered by the core — failure_halted_runs 29699 -> 49548 and closed_terminal_runs 50221 -> 30372. The lost-command minimized artifact changed because the deterministic shrinker's 1-minimal counterexample moved from `enqueue-close-b,shutdown` to `enqueue-close-b,inbound-close`; refrozen through the sanctioned US017_RETAIN=1 path. The other five minimized artifacts re-verified byte-identical. Driver/core equivalence on this path was probe-verified: four consecutive EOFs give actions 1,2,2,2 with STATE_VIOLATION from the second onward, IDENTICALLY for the bare core and for the driver, so the driver is now a faithful pass-through and the non-increment from the third onward is the core's own decision.

preregistered_plan.conformance: the exploration stays inside the plan bounds: 2 producer tasks (<= producer_tasks_max 3), 1 owner, command/write/event queue capacities 2/2/8 (<= 8), 12 actions per schedule (<= max_actions_per_schedule 64), preemption budget 3 (= preemption_bound), 79920 schedules (<= schedule_count_max 100000), 315070 enumeration branches (<= branch_count_max 1000000); the PRODUCER_ADMISSION_FAIRNESS_ABSENT stance is honored (queue-full refusals are final for that producer step, no retry fairness assumed) and the three weak-fairness assumptions gate only the final drain

bounds.program_shape: producer A [send_text, send_binary]; producer B [send_ping, send_close]; transport-read [inbound-ping, inbound-close, transport-eof]; transport-write [write-partial, write-all, write-all]; adapter-control [wake, shutdown]

adapter_model: the interpreter drives the public driver boundary exactly as the real adapter does: a surfaced DriverOutput::Failure HALTS the run at that instant (ws-testee io_loop maps it to LoopOutcome::ProtocolFailure and stops), so no schedule action, drain poll, or quiescence poll follows a Failure; Terminal-after-Failure is impossible by construction and additionally asserted

execution.replay_determinism: every schedule executed twice with FULL structured-trace equality: every poll record compares the input (kind + byte length), the complete typed input disposition (rejection details included), the complete command disposition (command payloads and typed rejection failures included), the complete owned output (semantic-event contents, typed failure values, byte-exact write suffixes), and the lifecycle state; the enumeration itself is re-run and compared; trace digests hash the full structured records plus the committed wire log
execution.terminal_disposition_exclusivity: asserted per run AND in aggregate, as an ORDERING property since the post-terminal ruling: surfaced failures total 49548 == failure_halted_runs (exactly one each, the halting failure); 30372 + 49548 == 79920; terminals total equals closed_terminal_runs plus the clean terminals of runs that later halted refusing post-convergence work; and no Terminal is ever observed after a surfaced Failure, checked against the ordered trace of every run

counters.reconciliation: clean-terminal runs reconcile EXACTLY per run (accepted == applied + rejected; the terminal_rejected term is gone because the driver no longer invents that verdict). Halted runs assert at-most-once disposition of accepted commands, with commands still queued at the halt belonging to the embedding adapter's teardown: aggregate applied 68144 + rejected 84866 = 153010 disposed of 199284 accepted, the 46274 remainder queued at halt boundaries and never double-disposed. The halted share grew with the repeated-EOF fix, which turns previously swallowed repeat notifications into surfaced refusals that stop their runs earlier

execution.outcome: PASS - zero invariant violations across all 79920 schedules

terminal_disposition_model: every full schedule ends in one of two typed dispositions, mirroring the real adapter: the clean Terminal from the absorbing Closed state (30372 runs), or the halt at the first surfaced fatal Failure (49548 runs, exactly one surfaced failure each) — the poisoned core retains its final state per the oracle's partial-execution semantics and the adapter stops there. Since owner decision us017-post-terminal-owner-decision-2026-08-28 these are ORDERED, not mutually exclusive: a schedule may converge cleanly, take its one Terminal, and then have further work pushed at the already-converged connection, which the core refuses — so a halted run may legitimately carry one preceding clean Terminal. The invariant that holds unconditionally is the ordering one: no Terminal is ever observed AFTER a surfaced Failure. Both classes fully quiesce, and clean-terminal runs reconcile every accepted command exactly once

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: this exploration, first execution against the batch-C driver
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::poll latched eof_applied=true even when the core refused the TransportEof with its NON-FATAL backpressure code (event queue congested), permanently losing the EOF: the connection stayed in Closing forever and no terminal was ever delivered
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: the EOF now stays latched on a non-fatal refusal and is retried on the next quiescent turn after outputs drain; fatal refusals still surface as a Failure output and latch
defects_found_and_fixed.red_evidence: both regression tests were executed against the pre-fix driver (fix stashed) and their failures were read; both pass with the fix restored

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: closure-commit review session 01a04533; reproduced RED by asserting terminal/failure exclusivity on the pre-fix interpreter
defects_found_and_fixed.description: the exploration interpreter kept driving a run after a surfaced DriverOutput::Failure, so schedules such as the minimized `shutdown,inbound-close` recorded BOTH a fatal Failure and a later Terminal while passing, invalidating the exclusive disposition oracle and the prior 732-run classification
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: adapter-faithful stop-on-Failure in the interpreter (no further schedule actions, drain, or quiescence polls after a Failure) plus the failure-halt-exclusivity invariant; the schedule space was reclassified and re-counted (52924 clean-terminal / 26996 failure-halted)
defects_found_and_fixed.note: harness fix, not a driver change; the shipped driver passes the corrected oracle on all schedules

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: routing the US-017 AC5 corpus differential harness through this driver, which moved the live-oracle-confirmed public transcript on us005.pub.0070
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::poll's latched-EOF arm set eof_applied=true WITHOUT calling the core once the core had converged on Closed, so ConnectionCore::handle_eof — which counts the action then refuses with STATE_VIOLATION — never ran. The connection silently swallowed an event shipped Java-WebSocket 1.6.0 reports as "eof repeated in CLOSED state".
defects_found_and_fixed.owner_ruling: us017-eof-after-closed-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha bd7849c3): driver defect; pass the EOF through. Corpus expectation NOT amended and transcript NOT re-baselined.

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: the sibling audit mandated by the eof-after-closed ruling, measured with a scratch probe rather than reasoned about
defects_found_and_fixed.description: after the once-only Terminal was delivered, the `!terminal_delivered` gate meant no branch of poll() ran, so poll returned the initial InputDisposition::Consumed{bytes:N} while the core never saw the bytes. Measured: Consumed{bytes:7} with counts.input_bytes 0 before and after. Reporting success for work never done, undetectable by any adapter — counts are not a usable detector either, because the core refuses a CLOSED-state byte input before accounting it.
defects_found_and_fixed.owner_ruling: us017-post-terminal-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha b52d244b), decision post-terminal-inbound: same ruling as the EOF defect; pass it through.

defects_found_and_fixed.description: the `&& !self.eof_applied` guard on the latched-EOF arm was set once and never cleared, so a REPEATED DriverInput::TransportEof (or a Shutdown after an applied EOF) never reached the core. the event-queue capacity used is 8, not the config floor 4: ConnectionCore::byte_input_event_bound needs 6 free slots to admit even a one-frame chunk, so floor-4 configurations can never make byte-path progress (recorded as an open config-floor observation, not changed by this closure)
